MCD.rationale: MCD's fundamental health is strong: Q1 2026 revenue +9.4% YoY to $6.52B, EPS +6.9% to $2.78, operating margin 45.2%, and $2.41B quarterly operating cash flow. The franchise model (95% franchised) generates best-in-class 46%+ operating margins with 18.2% ROIC. Global comp sales +3.8% and a 210M-user loyalty platform driving $40B in systemwide sales demonstrate durable competitive positioning. However, the balance sheet carries negative equity of -$1.29B with $61.3B in liabilities, creating structural fragility in a rising-rate environment (10Y at 4.57%, Baa spreads at 6.16%). Oil at $100/bbl (+51% in 3 months) is a direct input cost headwind and consumer spending pressure point, with the CEO himself flagging deteriorating conditions among lower-income families. Valuation is unmeasurable from supplied data (P/E series broken), but external sources suggest P/E ~23 at two-year lows with the stock down ~14-17% from highs — potentially offering a modest entry point for a quality franchise. The near-term catalyst is limited: Q2 guidance is for weaker sales due to lapping a prior-year promotion, and macro headwinds (oil, rates) show no sign of abating. On balance, excellent franchise quality and solid earnings trajectory are partially offset by macro headwinds, leveraged balance sheet risk, and consumer softness — warranting a mildly positive score.
